# Sources — `education:learning-materials-design`

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-sources.py from sources/*.toml. Do not edit. -->

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## Common Core State Standards — English Language Arts and Literacy

NGA Center for Best Practices & CCSSO · US · free to use with attribution — credit the publisher

<https://www.thecorestandards.org/ELA-Literacy/>

**Authoritative for:** Reading, writing, language and foundational-skills standards by grade — including the reading foundational skills that stop after grade 5, which is a common source of wrong alignment above it.

## DocsTeach

US National Archives and Records Administration · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.docsteach.org/>

**Authoritative for:** Primary-source documents for US history material, freely usable, organized for classroom activities rather than for archivists.

## International Literacy Association position statements and briefs

International Literacy Association · global · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.literacyworldwide.org/get-resources>

**Authoritative for:** Research-informed positions on phonics, phonemic awareness, comprehension and writing instruction — the evidence base a literacy product's claims are judged against.

## Library of Congress classroom materials

Library of Congress · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://www.loc.gov/classroom-materials/>

**Authoritative for:** Primary sources usable in published material without a rights problem, with teaching context already attached. The first place to look before licensing an image.

## NAEYC position statements, including Developmentally Appropriate Practice

National Association for the Education of Young Children · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.naeyc.org/resources/position-statements>

**Authoritative for:** What practice should look like for children under eight, and the statement most often cited when a task is challenged as too advanced. Not a standards document — it constrains method, not content.

## NCTM Principles and Standards and position statements

National Council of Teachers of Mathematics · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nctm.org/standards-and-positions/principles-and-standards/>

**Authoritative for:** The process standards — problem solving, reasoning and proof, communication, connections, representation — and the profession's position on what mathematics instruction should do. Some material requires membership.
